channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Shin Bet Chief orders personal protection for Gadi Eisenkot
item.description: Shin Bet chief David Zini approves a personal security detail for Gadi Eisenkot, while a decision on protection for Yair Golan remains pending.

item.title: 9-year-old boy pepper-sprayed in Jerusalem, suspect arrested
item.description: Police arrest a 22-year-old suspect over the pepper-spray attack on a nine-year-old Armenian Christian boy in Jerusalem's Mamilla neighborhood on Yom Kippur.

item.title: Ben-Gvir vows to see Hamas terrorist executed
item.description: Decades after protesting against Hassan Salameh’s deadly terror campaign, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir met the terrorist in prison and said he would work to see Hassan put to death.

item.title: Iran warns US of 'doomsday war,' claims it has changed military tactics
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi tells NBC that Tehran is prepared for a 'doomsday war' with the US but remains willing to pursue diplomacy.

item.title: Netanyahu's secret trip to Abu Dhabi to meet UAE President
item.description: Channel 12 reports Netanyahu secretly flew to Abu Dhabi for talks with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed; the Prime Minister's Office has not commented.

item.title: 'That's Me': Gazan student suspended after revealing role in massacre
item.description: Hussein Issa, a student who arrived in the Netherlands a few months ago, was suspended after revealing that he took part in the October 7th massacre.

item.title: Poll: Most Israelis support disqualification of Arab parties
item.description: Kan News poll gives Yashar 23 seats, Likud 21 and Bennett-Lapid 11, with both rival blocs tied at 52 seats just one month before Israel's elections.

item.title: Israel retaliates against Dutch boycott, revokes diplomats' immunity
item.description: Following the Dutch boycott of Israeli products, Sa'ar orders diplomats in Ramallah to surrender Israeli-issued documents within seven days.

item.title: Watch: Police drone records elimination of October 7th terrorist
item.description: New police footage shows the elimination of the terrorist accused of driving the motorcycle used to abduct Noa Argamani and Avinatan Or from the Nova festival.

item.title: From terror to diplomacy? Hamas offers to bring peace to Yemen
item.description: Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya offers to mediate Yemen's conflict, reveals repeated meetings with US officials, and outlines demands for Gaza's future.

item.title: Netanyahu takes aim at Erdogan: Israel preparing international legal case
item.description: Israel is reportedly compiling a legal case against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, focusing on his treatment of the Kurds and his ties to Hamas.

item.title: IDF general visits newtown in Binyamin region
item.description: Central Command chief Avi Bluth toured Metzukei Eretz with Binyamin leaders, meeting the 12 families who established the new community.

item.title: Report: Netanyahu instructs staff to prepare legal case against Turkish President
item.description: i24News reported on Sunday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has instructed his interministerial team and the director of the International Law Department at the Office of Legal Counsel and Legislative Affairs to prepare an international legal case against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

item.title: Yemeni military: Four Iranian drone and missile experts eliminated in Taizz
item.description: Yemeni military: Four Iranian drone and missile experts eliminated in Taizz

item.title: Listening devices suspected in Bnei Brak mayor’s office
item.description: A professional security sweep reportedly found signs that surveillance devices may have been installed in Mayor Hanoch Zeibert’s office.

item.title: Israeli Foreign Ministry: Closely monitoring situation of Israelis in Ethiopia amid unrest
item.description:
The Foreign Ministry announced that it is closely monitoring the situation of Israelis staying in areas of Ethiopia where security tensions have escalated.
"We are examining options for their departure in coordination with local authorities, in accordance with developments and security conditions on the ground," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

item.title: Trump expects more talks with Iran this week despite rejecting latest deal
item.description: Trump expects fresh negotiations with Iran this week despite rejecting Tehran's proposal, while keeping the possibility of further military strikes open.

item.title: Five arrested in suspected Iranian attempt to attack USAF base
item.description: Five men were arrested after three suspicious vans were spotted heading toward RAF Fairford, as British counter-terror police investigate a possible Iranian-linked terror plot.

item.title: 'Insane': Dutch boycott triggers checks on passengers arriving from Israel
item.description: Passengers arriving from Israel face additional baggage inspections at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport, with items from Judea and Samaria carrying jail time.

item.title: AI searches, deleted files raise questions in singer’s death
item.description: New findings in the investigation into Greek singer Giorgos Mazonakis’s death include AI searches about saving a patient, alerts from his treatment device, and deleted medical records and images recovered by investigators.

item.title: The Jewish Year art collection: Inner Lights
item.description: An artistic interpretation of the annual Jewish Holidays. Part 3 of 3.

item.description: Amb. Leiter: Neria's life still hangs in the balance

item.description: Jews are Jugglers: roots in the soil, eyes on the stars.

item.title: Report: Hezbollah still has not fully replaced Nasrallah
item.description: Two years after Nasrallah was killed, reports in Arab media point to the difficulty for Naim Qassem to fill the shoes of the leader who ruled for more than three decades.

item.title: Huckabee: US Embassy will have ‘forever home’ in Jerusalem
item.description: US Ambassador Mike Huckabee celebrates Sukkot in Jerusalem, declaring the city Israel’s eternal capital and discussing plans for a permanent US Embassy building.

item.title: Dozens of Israelis trapped in the Himalayas
item.description: Dozens of hikers were stuck in the village of Samgaon in Nepal, at an altitude of about 3,500 meters, after landslides and extreme weather blocked roads and bridges.

item.title: Historic synagogue auctioned for just one ruble
item.description: An old synagogue building in the city of Mariinsk, built in 1896 and later used as a sports club and a post office branch, will be offered for sale for pennies.

item.title: 'Rot in hell': Liri Albag reacts to captor's elimination
item.description: Liri Albag reacts to the elimination of Muhamma Gabain, who held her and eight other Israelis hostage in Gaza.

item.title: Israel election ballot letters revealed
item.description: Bennett, Netanyahu, Ben Gvir and Golan will all run under distinctive Hebrew letters. One party’s request was rejected because it was considered a name of God.

item.title: 'Your heart just sinks': Terror victim recounts learning friend was hurt
item.description: Still recovering from a ramming attack, Ofir Engelsman visits the site where childhood friend Neria Leiter was wounded in a similar attack, calling for a new security approach.
